extraction.name: OpenBookQA
extraction.description: OpenBookQA is a new kind of question answering dataset modeled after open book exams for assessing human understanding of a subject. It consists of about 6000 4-way multiple-choice questions and a set of 1326 elementary level science facts (the 'open book'). Questions probe an understanding of these facts and their application to novel situations, requiring combining an open book fact with broad common knowledge obtained from other sources. Human performance is close to 92%.
extraction.creator: Todor Mihaylov, Peter Clark, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal (Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence; Research Training Group AIPHES & Heidelberg University)
extraction.citeAs: Mihaylov, T., Clark, P., Khot, T., & Sabharwal, A. (2018). Can a Suit of Armor Conduct Electricity? A New Dataset for Open Book Question Answering. arXiv:1809.02789v1 [cs.CL].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were created via a multi-stage crowdsourcing and partial expert filtering process. Crowd-workers were shown a random science fact from the open book set F, asked to think of a second common fact that may be combined with it, then convert the combination into a 4-way multiple-choice question. Questions were filtered for hardness using an IR solver and a word association solver, then verified for answerability by 5 new crowd-workers. The Dev and Test splits were further filtered by an in-house expert to ensure higher quality.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: TableILP did not answer 24% of the OpenBookQA questions at all due to missing knowledge in its small set of knowledge tables.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The core science facts (open book F) are a subset of the WorldTree corpus (Jansen et al., 2018), specifically 1326 facts filtered from 2287 WorldTree facts marked as 'central' in at least one explanation. Questions were generated by crowd-workers based on these facts. An auxiliary set K of about 6000 additional facts was also collected from crowd-workers.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Answer choices of each question were randomly shuffled to avoid unintended bias (Choice 'A' was the correct answer in 69% of questions before shuffling). Questions were filtered to exclude negation words and to enforce uniform answer choice length (all with at most 3 or at least 4 words).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The question generation pipeline included: (1) basic checks for exactly 4 answer choices, no negation words, and uniform answer choice length; (2) automatic hardness filter requiring that neither an IR solver nor a word association solver answers correctly and the top 3 IR retrieved sentences are insufficient; (3) crowd answerability filter requiring at least 4 out of 5 workers to answer correctly; (4) random shuffling of answer choices; (5) expert filtering for Dev and Test splits. Overall, 8140 questions were collected, of which 2183 were discarded in the answerability filtering step.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd-workers (Amazon Mechanical Turk, North America, 'masters' level qualification) were shown a science fact, asked to think of a second common fact, combine them into a new assertion, and write a 4-way multiple-choice question. Five new crowd-workers then answered each question to verify answerability (at least 4 out of 5 must answer correctly). Workers also marked a second fact k needed for each question. Dev and Test sets were additionally reviewed by an in-house expert (Madeleine van Zuylen) for higher quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human accuracy was estimated using a statistical model: each question has an unknown human accuracy pq (probability a random human answers correctly). The empirical estimate uses the 5 annotations from the answerability verification step. Hoeffding's Inequality was applied to show convergence; the conservative lower bound H(Q) - 3% with probability over 98.8% is reported. Additional validation was performed by obtaining 5 new annotations for 100 randomly chosen questions from each of Train, Dev, and Test sets, yielding 88.6%, 90.2%, and 91.6% respectively.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 5 crowd-worker annotations per question for answerability verification
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers from North America with 'masters' level qualification
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: IR solver (Clark et al., 2016), word association based solver (Turney, 2017), TfIdfVectorizer from scikit-learn for knowledge retrieval
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: OpenBookQA is designed to advance research in question answering that requires multi-hop reasoning and integration of external common knowledge, moving beyond simple pattern matching. It highlights the gap between human performance (~92%) and state-of-the-art AI systems (~50%), motivating further research in knowledge retrieval and reasoning for AI systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Human bias is present in the crowdsourced dataset, as evidenced by simple neural baselines (plausible answer detector ignoring the question, odd-one-out solver) achieving ~50% accuracy. Workers generally start with the correct answer and create three incorrect ones, which tend to be homogeneous or share common properties uncharacteristic of the correct answer. In 21% of analyzed training questions, the crowdsourced question tests for a fact that doesn't necessarily need the original science fact. The auxiliary set K of second facts is noted to be often incomplete, over-complete, or only distantly related to the question.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The auxiliary set K of second facts should not be viewed as 'gold' additional facts or as a substitute for broad common knowledge, as they were often incomplete, over-complete, or only distantly related to questions. The dataset is limited to elementary level science topics. Some questions fall outside the science domain. The oracle f+k model still only achieves ~76% accuracy, indicating non-trivial reasoning challenges remain even with gold facts provided.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Development (validation), and Testing of question answering systems. The dataset is intended for research on open book question answering requiring multi-hop reasoning, knowledge retrieval, and integration of external common knowledge. For Train and Dev questions, the associated core science fact f is included as intermediate supervision signal. The dataset and model code are available at http://data.allenai.org/OpenBookQA.
